history.summary: Artra 2BR+study, 829 sqft, $2.00M / $2,413 psf — a 2021 99LH mixed-use tower literally on top of Redhill MRT (61-80m, retail podium). Against same-vintage D03 peers the ask is fair to mildly cheap (age-adjusted district median $2,492; same-TOP-year Stirling Residences prints $2,478), and the project's downside record is spotless — 89 profitable exits, 0 unprofitable. But the forward case is ordinary: floor-matched resale-to-resale evidence for this exact layout runs ~3.0-3.3%/yr, not the 4.97% 5yr CAGR the algo scores; net yield is 2.2%; 190 of 400 units are this same 786-829 sqft layout; and $2.0M sits exactly at the HDB-upgrader ceiling that supplies a third of Artra's buyers. Safe and liquid, not lucrative.
history.rating_rationale: Fairly priced, highly liquid, low-downside — but no measurable forward edge at this ask. (1) VALUE IS FAIR, NOT CHEAP. The ask is -3.2% vs the age-adjusted D03 median and -0.7% vs new-launch-implied fair value, yet +2.5% above Artra's own 24-month same-size median ($2,353 psf, n=19) and ~2% above the most recent identical 829 sqft print ($1.96M / $2,365 psf, 7 Jul 2026). Cheap-vs-peers is the strongest measured forward signal and here it is roughly zero. (2) THE APPRECIATION INPUT IS OVERSTATED. The algo scores a 4.97%/yr 5yr CAGR (77 txns), but that series is 37/77 sub-sales from the 2021-23 launch-premium convergence. Floor-matched resale-to-resale for the 829 sqft layout: Apr-24 $1.960M (36-40F) -> May-26 $2.100M (36-40F) = +3.3%/yr; Jul-24 $1.950M (26-30F) -> Mar-26 $2.050M (31-35F) = +3.0%/yr; mid-floor Aug-24 $1.920M -> Aug-25 $1.938M = +0.9%/yr. ~3.2%/yr is the honest number, and it sits below the RCR realized forward baseline (+3.1%) and well below OCR (+3.7%). Rescoring at 3.2% drops score_1000 740 -> 674. (3) THIN CARRY. 3.6% gross / 2.2% net on a $6,000-6,200 rent (Jun-26 2BR prints $6,000-6,500) — carry-negative on leverage at current rates, and all-cash 5yr ROI lands ~3.5-3.8%/yr, i.e. the roi_sensitivity DOWNSIDE case is the base case. With ABSD 20% on a second property (not in the $73.1k entry costs) the 5yr return falls to ~1.5-2%/yr and the case fails outright. (4) EXIT COMPETITION IS STRUCTURAL. 190 of 400 units (47.5%) are the same 786-829 sqft 2BR+study; ~11 of them print per year; five Artra 2BR asks are live right now. This one is the cheapest live ask by psf and has still sat unchanged at $2.00M since 7 Jun 2026 (relisted 21 Jul from id 500082338, ~7 weeks) while a cheaper identical 829 sqft unit transacted on 7 Jul. (5) AFFORDABILITY CEILING. 33% of Artra's buyers are HDB upgraders whose band tops out ~$1.8-2.0M; the ask is at that wall, so the 5yr ROI projection's $2.51M exit ($3,030 psf for an 829 sqft leasehold 2BR) requires a buyer pool Artra has not historically drawn on. WHAT SUPPORTS IT: 61m to Redhill MRT with an integrated retail podium is top-decile connectivity and the most durable non-value signal measured (as-of-T std_beta -0.11); liquidity is genuinely deep (489 total txns, 50+ in the past year, 400 units, 91yrs lease left); realsmart shows 100% profitable across 89 exits with $40.7M total profits and a 5.7yr average hold. That is a real capital-preservation floor. But REALSCORE is only 3.2/5 and just 2 of 89 exits beat 6% annualized — the record says 'nobody loses money here', not 'this compounds'. A fair price on a safe asset with a ~3%/yr forward rate and 2.2% net carry is the definition of Neutral. NOTE: this supersedes the 2026-06-08 Buy (high) on this same unit at this same price — that call credited the 4.97% trailing CAGR as a forward edge (backtested ~0 forward power) and read the ask as a discount to a $2,507 median when it is a +2.5% premium to the project's own same-size prints.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid and well-evidenced, but the yield is carry, never appreciation. 829 sqft 2BR+study with 2 baths is the deepest-demand private rental format in the Redhill/Alexandra corridor, and the volume is real: 57 rental contracts at Artra in the past month, latest-12 median $6,400 (range $5,600-$9,000), with Jun-2026 800-900 sqft contracts printing $6,000, $6,000 and $6,500. The $6,000/mo estimate (ura_project_bed, confidence 0.95) is right, arguably $100-200 conservative. That is 3.6% gross but only 2.2% net after MCST, property tax, agency and the 15% marginal tax on letting profit — positive all-cash, negative on a mortgage at current rates. Tenant demand is anchored by 1-min MRT access to the CBD and the retail podium, and the corridor's employment catchment (Alexandra/Mapletree Business City, Harbourfront) is stable. Risk is on the supply side rather than demand: 190 near-identical units in the same building compete for the same tenant, which caps rent escalation to roughly the market rate — assume ~2%/yr, not more. At 3.6% gross the yield is mid-band, so it neither earns a bonus nor triggers the high-yield-predicts-lower-growth penalty (std_beta -0.16); treat it as adequate carry that does not rescue a thin capital return.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: ~3.2%/yr is the honest forward rate, against the 4.97% the algo scores. The 77-transaction URA series is 37 sub-sales and 40 resales, and the sub-sale half spans Jun-2021 ($1,840-1,967 psf) to Dec-2023 ($2,265 psf) — that ramp is launch-premium convergence after the 2020/21 TOP, not repeatable capital growth, exactly the new-launch inflation the priors warn against. Stripping to resale-to-resale on the subject's own 829 sqft layout with floor bands held constant: Apr-24 $1.960M (36-40F) -> May-26 $2.100M (36-40F) = +7.1% over 25 months = +3.3%/yr; Jul-24 $1.950M (26-30F) -> Mar-26 $2.050M (31-35F) = +3.0%/yr on a slight floor upgrade; and the cleanest same-band pair, Aug-24 $1.920M (16-20F) -> Aug-25 $1.938M (16-20F), is just +0.9%/yr. The project's annual medians tell the same story of deceleration: 2023 $2,274 -> 2024 $2,353 (+3.5%) -> 2025 $2,374 (+0.9%) -> 2026 $2,477 (+4.3%), a 3-year compound of ~2.9%/yr. Realsmart's own 'avg annualized profit, past 1y' of 4.2% is measured over an average 5.7yr hold that includes the same launch ramp. I set an override of 3.2%/yr, which is where the floor-matched resale evidence converges and which sits just above the RCR realized forward baseline (+3.1%) — justified by the MRT integration, discounted by the affordability ceiling. There is no dated catalyst to add: the nearest future station (Havelock, TEL) is 1,267m and future-infrastructure scores have no measured forward power. The binding constraint is quantum, not location — at $2.0M this layout is already at the top of the $1.8-2.0M HDB-upgrader band that supplies a third of Artra's buyers, so the next leg has to come from a thinner private-to-private pool. Stacked Homes reaches the same conclusion independently: gains 'more steady rather than a dramatic surge, as affordability limits are starting to bite'.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: UNKNOWN — and this is the single biggest gap in the call. No profile exists for Artra (stack_profile: not_researched), the DB record carries no floor or facing, and a re-fetch of the listing returned Cloudflare 403, so the storey could not be resolved. It matters more here than usual, because Artra's 44-storey tower shows a wide, clean floor gradient within the identical 828.8 sqft layout: 6-15F cleared $1.869-1.990M, 16-25F cleared $1.910-1.938M, and 31-45F cleared $2.050-2.100M (Mar-26 and May-26). Against that, the $2.00M ask is ~3-5% ABOVE where mid- and low-floor 829s have been clearing, but 2-5% BELOW the two 2026 high-floor prints. If this is a 31F+ unit the ask is defensible and the call would firm toward Buy; if it is below the 25th floor it is simply over-asked and the call firms toward Avoid. Neutral is the correct rating under that unresolved spread, and the cheapest way to resolve it is a single question to the agent about the storey and facing. On facing: the 786-829 sqft 2BR+study is the project's dominant type (190 of 400 units) and marketing for the stack describes a north-south orientation with no west sun, which if true for this unit removes the main afternoon-heat concern in the corridor — unverified for this specific listing. Note also that all units front a mixed-use podium above an MRT station: low floors carry real road and rail noise from Alexandra Road and the EWL viaduct, so a low-floor unit would be doubly penalized on both price and livability.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale, size- and floor-matched on the subject's own 828.8 sqft layout from data/ura_district_D03.csv (41 prints of the 786-829 sqft type, Jun-2021 to May-2026): Apr-24 $1.960M (36-40F) -> May-26 $2.100M (36-40F) = +3.3%/yr; Jul-24 $1.950M (26-30F) -> Mar-26 $2.050M (31-35F) = +3.0%/yr; Aug-24 $1.920M (16-20F) -> Aug-25 $1.938M (16-20F) = +0.9%/yr. Cross-checked against Artra's annual project medians (2023 $2,274 -> 2026 $2,477 psf = +2.9%/yr compound, realsmart.sg/p/artra, data through 7 Jul 2026) and the RCR realized forward baseline (+3.1%/yr). Excludes the 37 sub-sale prints in the URA series, which capture 2021-23 launch-premium convergence rather than resale appreciation, and which are what lifts the raw 5yr CAGR to 4.97%.
